text: When the kinetic energy of an electron is increased nine times, the wavelength of the de-Broglie wave associated with it would become :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$λ=\dfrac{h}{p}$ and $p=\sqrt{2mK}$, so $λ=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, i.e. $λ\propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{K}}$.

With $K^{'}=9K$: $\dfrac{λ^{'}}{λ}=\sqrt{\dfrac{K}{9K}}=\dfrac{1}{3}$.

The de Broglie wavelength becomes one-third of its original value.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Which of the following is the plot of Gibb's free energy (G) vs temperature (T), at constant pressure, for a pure substance?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For a pure substance, $dG=VdP-SdT$.

At constant pressure ($dP=0$): $\left (\dfrac{𝜕G}{𝜕T}\right )_{P}=-S$.

The entropy of a substance is always positive ($S>0$), so the slope of the $G$ vs $T$ plot is negative.

Thus $G$ decreases as $T$ increases: only the first graph (a line falling with $T$) fits; the rising lines need $S<0$ and the horizontal line needs $S=0$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
For Periodic Table which of the following statements are TRUE

A. Shielding increases as we go down in the group.

B. Shielding increases sharply across the period.

C. Ionization enthalpy increases down the group.

D. Metallic character increases down the group.

E. Electronegativity decreases down the group.

Choose the correct answer from the following options :
options: A, C, D and E only
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement A is true: down a group the number of inner electron shells increases, so the shielding of the valence electrons increases.

Statement B is false: across a period electrons enter the same shell and shield one another poorly, so shielding increases only slightly while the effective nuclear charge increases.

Statement C is false: ionisation enthalpy decreases down a group because atomic size and shielding increase.

Statement D is true: down a group atomic size increases, the valence electrons are lost more easily and metallic character increases.

Statement E is true: down a group the larger atom attracts the shared electron pair less strongly, so electronegativity decreases.

The true statements are therefore A, D and E, and options (B) and (D) both give exactly this set.

Hence, the correct options are (B) and (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The correct option for relative covalent nature of compounds is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Fajans' rules: covalent character increases with higher charge and smaller size of the cation and with larger size of the anion.

$\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$ (higher charge, smaller size) polarises $\mathrm{Cl}^{-}$ more than $\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$, so $\mathrm{SnCl}_{4}>\mathrm{SnCl}_{2}$ is correct.

$\mathrm{I}^{-}$ is larger and more polarisable than $\mathrm{F}^{-}$, so $\mathrm{KI}>\mathrm{KF}$.

$\mathrm{Li}^{+}$ is smaller than $\mathrm{K}^{+}$, so $\mathrm{LiF}>\mathrm{KF}$.

HCl is a covalent molecule while NaCl is ionic, so $\mathrm{HCl}>\mathrm{NaCl}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The $E^{\circ }$ (volt) values are : $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}/\mathrm{Al}$, $-1.66$, $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}/\mathrm{Sc}$, $-2.08$, $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}/\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$, $+0.77$, $\mathrm{Hg}_{2}^{2+}/\mathrm{Hg}$, $+0.79$. Arrangement of cations, $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ and $\mathrm{Hg}_{2}^{2+}$ in decreasing order of oxidizing strength is
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The more positive the standard reduction potential, the greater the tendency of the cation to be reduced, i.e. the stronger it is as an oxidising agent.

$E^{\circ }$: $\mathrm{Hg}_{2}^{2+}$ ($+0.79$) $>$ $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ ($+0.77$) $>$ $\mathrm{Al}^{3+}$ ($-1.66$) $>$ $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ ($-2.08$).

Oxidising strength: $\mathrm{Hg}_{2}^{2+}>\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}>\mathrm{Al}^{3+}>\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: In low and high spin octahedral $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$ complexes the number of electrons in $t_{2g}$ level respectively will be . (given At. no. of Co, 27)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Co ($Z=27$): $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{7}4s^{2}$; $\mathrm{Co}^{3+}$: $3d^{6}$.

Low spin ($\Delta _{o}>P$): all six electrons pair in $t_{2g}$, $t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{0}$, so 6 electrons in $t_{2g}$.

High spin ($\Delta _{o}<P$): $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$, so 4 electrons in $t_{2g}$.

text: Glycerol can be separated from spent-lye on industrial scale by using
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Glycerol has a high boiling point (about 563 K) and decomposes at or below its normal boiling point.

Under reduced pressure a liquid boils at a lower temperature, so glycerol distils without decomposition from the spent lye of the soap industry.

TLC is an analytical (small-scale) technique, crystallisation needs a solid, and glycerol is miscible with water, so differential extraction does not work.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Which of the following is unstable?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) Cyclobutadiene: cyclic, planar and fully conjugated with $4π$ electrons ($4n$, $n=1$), so it is antiaromatic and highly unstable.

(B) Cyclopentadienyl anion: $6π$ electrons ($4n+2$, $n=1$) in a planar conjugated ring, so aromatic and stable.

(C) Cycloheptatriene: has an $sp^{3}$ $\mathrm{CH}_{2}$ group, so it is non-aromatic, but it is an ordinary stable compound.

(D) Benzene: $6π$ electrons, aromatic and very stable.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
Major product of the following reaction is


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The reactant is 3,3-dimethylpent-4-enoic acid, $\mathrm{CH}_{2}=\mathrm{CH}-\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}-\mathrm{CH}_{2}-\mathrm{COOH}$; $\mathrm{NaHCO}_{3}$ converts it into the carboxylate ion.

$\mathrm{I}_{2}$ adds to the C=C to give a cyclic iodonium ion.

The carboxylate oxygen attacks the internal carbon (C-4) of the iodonium ion intramolecularly (iodolactonisation); a five-membered ring closes faster than a six-membered one.

Product: a γ-lactone, 5-(iodomethyl)-4,4-dimethyloxolan-2-one, with $\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{I}$ on the ring carbon next to the ring oxygen.

The open-chain iodo acids would need addition of HI, which is not the reagent here, and the six-membered δ-lactone is the minor ring size.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: Which one of the following compounds can be prepared in good yield by Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Hoffmann bromamide degradation: $\mathrm{RCONH}_{2}+\mathrm{Br}_{2}+4\mathrm{NaOH}\to \mathrm{RNH}_{2}+\mathrm{Na}_{2}\mathrm{CO}_{3}+2\mathrm{NaBr}+2\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$.

It gives only primary amines, with one carbon atom less than the amide.

$\mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{CONH}_{2}\to \mathrm{C}_{6}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{NH}_{2}$: aniline is obtained in good yield.

Phenylacetamide and benzamide are amides (starting materials, not products), and N-methylaniline is a secondary amine, which this reaction cannot give.

text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Glycogen is highly branched polysaccharide and commonly known as animal starch due to its similarity with amylopectin.

Statement II: Amylose is water insoluble and constitutes about 15-20% of starch.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Statement I is correct: glycogen, the storage carbohydrate of animals, has a structure similar to amylopectin but is even more highly branched, hence it is called animal starch.

Statement II is incorrect: amylose is the water-soluble component of starch (about 15–20%); amylopectin (about 80–85%) is insoluble in water.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: In the ring test of $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$ ion what is the oxidation number of iron in the complex (brown ring) $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{5}\mathrm{NO}]\mathrm{SO}_{4}$ ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the brown ring test, $\mathrm{NO}_{3}^{-}$ is reduced by $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ to NO, which binds to iron as the nitrosonium ion, $\mathrm{NO}^{+}$ (an electron passes from NO to Fe).

The complex ion is $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O})_{5}(\mathrm{NO})]^{2+}$ (balanced by $\mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-}$), and $\mathrm{H}_{2}\mathrm{O}$ is neutral.

$x+5(0)+(+1)=+2\Rightarrow x=+1$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The density of 4 molal solution of NaOH is $1.160\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mL}^{-1}$. The molarity of the solution is $________ M. ($Given : Molar mass of NaOH $=40\mathrm{g}~\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$) (nearest integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
4 molal: 4 mol NaOH ($4\times 40=160\mathrm{g}$) in $1000\mathrm{g}$ water.

Mass of solution $=1000+160=1160\mathrm{g}$.

Volume of solution $=\dfrac{1160}{1.160}=1000\mathrm{mL}=1\mathrm{L}$.

Molarity $=\dfrac{4\mathrm{mol}}{1\mathrm{L}}=4\mathrm{M}$.

text:
31 g of ethylene glycol is mixed with 500 g of water. The freezing point of the aqueous solution is $________ K$.

(in nearest integer)

($K_{f}$ of water $=1.86\mathrm{K}\mathrm{kg}\qquad \mathrm{mol}^{-1}$)

sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Ethylene glycol $\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{6}\mathrm{O}_{2}$: $M=62\mathrm{g}\mathrm{mol}^{-1}$, so $n=\dfrac{31}{62}=0.5\mathrm{mol}$.

Molality $m=\dfrac{0.5}{0.5\mathrm{kg}}=1\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{kg}^{-1}$ (non-electrolyte, $i=1$).

$\Delta T_{f}=K_{f}m=1.86\times 1=1.86\mathrm{K}$.

$T_{f}=273.15-1.86=271.29\mathrm{K}\approx 271\mathrm{K}$.

text:
50 mL of 0.1 M $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$ is titrated against 0.1 M NaOH solution. When 10 mL of NaOH is added, the pH of the solution becomes $________$ $\times 10^{-1}$. (nearest integer)

Given: p$K_{a}$ ($\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}$) = 4.8, log 2 = 0.3
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}=50\times 0.1=5\mathrm{mmol}$; NaOH $=10\times 0.1=1\mathrm{mmol}$.

After neutralisation: $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOH}=4\mathrm{mmol}$, $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COONa}=1\mathrm{mmol}$ (acidic buffer).

$\mathrm{pH}=\mathrm{p}K_{a}+\log \dfrac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}=4.8+\log \dfrac{1}{4}$.

$\mathrm{pH}=4.8-2(0.3)=4.2=42\times 10^{-1}$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: For the given cell $\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{s})|\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{C}_{1}\mathrm{M})||\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{M})|\mathrm{Zn}(\mathrm{s})$ the change in Gibbs energy ($\Delta G$) will be zero when $\dfrac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}$ is equal to $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
This is a concentration cell: $E_{\text{cell}}^{\circ }=0$; cell reaction $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{C}_{2})\to \mathrm{Zn}^{2+}(\mathrm{C}_{1})$, $n=2$.

$E_{\text{cell}}=0-\dfrac{0.059}{2}\log \dfrac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}$.

$\Delta G=-nFE_{\text{cell}}=0$ requires $E_{\text{cell}}=0$, i.e. $\log \dfrac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}=0$.

$\dfrac{C_{1}}{C_{2}}=1$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
$\mathrm{X}\to \mathrm{Y}+\mathrm{Z}$

X decomposes at 700 K to give Y and Z. The results of two measurements are :

Initial concentration of X / (mol/L)6.012.0Half life / s1.02.0
The rate constant for the reaction is $________ ($in appropriate unit)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For an $n$th-order reaction $t_{1/2}\propto [\mathrm{X}]_{0}^{1-n}$.

Doubling $[\mathrm{X}]_{0}$ (6.0 to 12.0) doubles $t_{1/2}$ (1.0 to 2.0 s), so $1-n=1$, $n=0$ (zero order).

Zero order: $t_{1/2}=\dfrac{[\mathrm{X}]_{0}}{2k}$, so $k=\dfrac{6.0}{2\times 1.0}=3.0\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{L}^{-1}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$.

Check: $\dfrac{12.0}{2\times 2.0}=3.0$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
Consider the molecules / ions given below

$\mathrm{XeO}_{3}$, $\mathrm{BF}_{4}^{-}$, $\mathrm{I}_{3}^{-}$, $\mathrm{SF}_{6}$, $\mathrm{PCl}_{5}$

The ratio of number of molecules having $sp^{3}d$ hybridisation to those having $sp^{3}$ hybridisation is $________$
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Steric number = atoms bonded to the central atom + lone pairs on it.

$\mathrm{XeO}_{3}$: 3 + 1 = 4, $sp^{3}$; $\mathrm{BF}_{4}^{-}$: 4 + 0 = 4, $sp^{3}$.

$\mathrm{I}_{3}^{-}$: 2 + 3 = 5, $sp^{3}d$; $\mathrm{PCl}_{5}$: 5 + 0 = 5, $sp^{3}d$.

$\mathrm{SF}_{6}$: 6 + 0 = 6, $sp^{3}d^{2}$.

Ratio $=\dfrac{2(sp^{3}d)}{2(sp^{3})}=1$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
The number of coloured and paramagnetic ions from the following in aqueous solution are $________$.

$\mathrm{Ti}^{3+}$, $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$, $\mathrm{Ti}^{4+}$, $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$

Given Atomic no.

Sc, 21; Ti, 22; Co, 27; Ni, 28; Cu, 29; Zn, 30
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Colour (d–d transition) and paramagnetism both need unpaired d electrons.

$\mathrm{Ti}^{3+}$ $3d^{1}$ (1 unpaired, purple), $\mathrm{Co}^{2+}$ $3d^{7}$ (3 unpaired, pink), $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ $3d^{8}$ (2 unpaired, green), $\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}$ $3d^{9}$ (1 unpaired, blue): coloured and paramagnetic.

$\mathrm{Cu}^{+}$ and $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}$ ($3d^{10}$), $\mathrm{Ti}^{4+}$ and $\mathrm{Sc}^{3+}$ ($3d^{0}$): no unpaired electron, colourless and diamagnetic.

Number of coloured and paramagnetic ions = 4.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text: The number of isomeric compounds (structural isomers only) possible with the molecular formula $\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_{2}$, which do not react with metallic sodium is $________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\mathrm{C}_{5}\mathrm{H}_{10}\mathrm{O}_{2}$ (one degree of unsaturation): carboxylic acids react with Na (acidic H), esters $\mathrm{RCOOR}^{'}$ have no acidic H and do not.

Formates $\mathrm{HCOOC}_{4}\mathrm{H}_{9}$: n-butyl, isobutyl, sec-butyl, tert-butyl = 4.

Acetates $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{COOC}_{3}\mathrm{H}_{7}$: n-propyl, isopropyl = 2.

Propanoate: $\mathrm{C}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}\mathrm{COOC}_{2}\mathrm{H}_{5}$ = 1.

Methyl esters: $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOCH}_{3}$, $(\mathrm{CH}_{3})_{2}\mathrm{CHCOOCH}_{3}$ = 2.

Number of esters $=4+2+1+2=9$.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift

text:
Among the following, how many hydrocarbon (s) with formula $\mathrm{C}_{10}\mathrm{H}_{16}$ which on reaction with acidic potassium permanganate yield(s) same product ? $________$


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Number the structures I to V from left to right. I (cyclohexane ring + one C=C) is $\mathrm{C}_{10}\mathrm{H}_{18}$ and V has only nine carbons ($\mathrm{C}_{9}\mathrm{H}_{14}$); only II, III and IV are $\mathrm{C}_{10}\mathrm{H}_{16}$.

Acidic $\mathrm{KMnO}_{4}$ cleaves every C=C: $=\mathrm{CH}_{2}\to \mathrm{CO}_{2}$, $=\mathrm{CH}-\to -\mathrm{COOH}$, $=\mathrm{C}(\mathrm{R})-\to >\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{O}$.

II (ring C=C between two CH carbons) gives $\mathrm{HOOC}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_{3})-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{COOH})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$.

III (1,2-dimethyl-3-allylcyclopentene) gives $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$.

IV (ring C=C at the methyl-bearing carbon) gives $\mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CO}-\mathrm{CH}(\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COOH})-\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{COCH}_{3}$.

III and IV give the same product (3-acetyl-6-oxoheptanoic acid, with $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$), so the number is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 30th July Evening Shift
